question: In patients with newly diagnosed rheumatoid arthritis who have no contraindications, methotrexate is recommended as the first-line disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD) before initiating biologic therapy.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Methotrexate is the cornerstone first-line DMARD for RA per ACR and EULAR guidelines. Biologic agents are reserved for patients with inadequate response or intolerance to conventional DMARDs such as methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, and sulfasalazine.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. ACR/EULAR guidelines recommend methotrexate as anchor DMARD therapy in RA. Biologics (TNF inhibitors, IL-6 inhibitors) are added or substituted only when methotrexate at adequate dose (≥15–25 mg/week with folate supplementation) fails to achieve the treatment target.
